items.title: Battle to be mayor a ‘clear two-way race’ in Mississauga, candidate says
items.summary: The field is set for the mayoral race in Mississauga, with more than a dozen candidates preparing to do battle until voters make the final decision on Oct. 26. m. deadline to register for the 2026 municipal election, 14 names appeared on the list of hopefuls looking to occupy the mayor’s seat in Canada’s seventh-largest city for the next term of council. The two highest-profile candidates — the current mayor, Carolyn Parrish, and her predecessor, Bonnie Crombie — are joined in the contest by city councillors Alvin Tedjo (Ward 2) and Dipika Damerla (Ward 7) and 10 others of varying experience in the realm of political campaigning. ” Crombie, who left the Mississauga mayor’s post in 2024 after 10 years to lead the Ontario Liberals and take a shot at unseating the premier, said she’s looking to reclaim the seat because she believes better days are ahead for the city. “Everywhere I go, I hear the same concerns,” Crombie said in a news release on Friday. “Life has become too expensive. People are worried about safety. Traffic and congestion are taking too much time away from families. And residents want to know that City Hall is focused on getting things done. “I’m running because I believe Mississauga can do better,” she continued.

items.title: House of the week: Family home on a quiet Mississauga street
items.summary: This place: A large family home on a quiet street in Mississauga. Bedrooms: Four plus three in the basement Features: This family home is nestled on a quiet cul-de-sac in Erindale. The home offers over 5,200 square feet of finished living space and is designed for multi-generational living. Features include wainscoting, hardwood flooring, pot lights and expansive windows throughout. On the main floor, find combined living and dining rooms and a main-floor office. The kitchen overlooks the breakfast area and the spacious family room is complete with built-in cabinetry, a fireplace and views of the backyard. Upstairs, find four bedrooms with vaulted ceilings and custom closets. The primary bedroom offers dual walk-in closets, a six-piece ensuite bathroom, a fireplace and a sitting area. The additional bedrooms enjoy ensuite bathroom access. The basement has a separate entrance and a self-contained three-bedroom suite featuring two full bathrooms, living areas, a recreation space, a wine cellar, a cold room and storage. The Queensway corridor can be accessed through a rear gate to reach nearby walking and cycling trails, Huron Park, a community centre, Trillium Hospital and everyday amenities.

items.title: Your southern Ontario weekend forecast: storms, rain and a cool-down
items.summary: A beautiful Friday will give way to a miserable Saturday and Sunday, Environment Canada says. A cloudy, rainy weekend is expected in Ontario. Southern Ontario is in for a stormy weekend of Aug. 22 and 23, with showers, thunderstorms and wind gusts of up to 80 km/h forecast across the region, Environment and Climate Change Canada says. Rainfall of 15 to 30 millimetres is expected for most areas, with the worst conditions arriving Saturday for the southwest and Sunday for eastern Ontario, including Ottawa. Environment and Climate Change meteorologist Jean-Philippe Bégin said cloudiness will increase Friday night due to the arrival of low-pressure system. Clouds will arrive in the Windsor area first and move across southern Ontario. Toronto could still see some sunny breaks early Saturday morning, but by late morning clouds will move in. “Then it’s showers and thunderstorms for the rest of the day,” Bégin said. Windsor will likely see showers and thunderstorms the entire day, while regions further east, such as Toronto, might see them by the afternoon and evening.

items.title: Mohawk Saint Kateri Tekakwitha Lends Her Name to a New Churchill Meadows Catholic School
items.summary: According to INsauga, a new French-language Catholic elementary school in Mississauga's Churchill Meadows neighbourhood will open its doors to nearly 300 students this fall, carrying the name of one of the most significant Indigenous figures in Catholic history. Ecole elementaire catholique Sainte-Kateri-Tekakwitha, located at 5450 Festival Drive, welcomes its first students on September 8 with space for 294 elementary students and 73 licensed child care spaces for children from three months to four years old. INsauga reports the project was funded by the Ontario government and is one of 35 new or expanded schools opening across the province for the 2026-27 school year. The school marks the fourth Catholic French-language elementary school in Mississauga operated by Conseil scolaire catholique MonAvenir, according to the outlet, with the board saying the new facility responds to the city's growing Francophone population. INsauga notes the school's namesake, Kateri Tekakwitha, was a Mohawk woman born in 1656 who converted to Catholicism and was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI in 2012, becoming the first Indigenous woman in North America declared a saint by the Catholic Church.

items.title: Peel Police Sign Binding Deal for Outside Oversight of Anti-Racism Reforms
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Regional Police have entered a new binding agreement with the Ontario Human Rights Commission and the Peel Police Service Board that introduces independent oversight to check whether recommended anti-racism reforms are actually being carried out. The outlet reports the arrangement, announced August 18, comes after years of concern over systemic racism within the force and as disparities in policing involving Black residents have persisted. Mississauga.com cites Peel Regional Police data showing Black residents experienced use of force at nearly three times their share of the region's population. The agreement builds on recommendations from the Human Rights Project, a review launched in 2020 to address systemic racism in Peel Region, according to the outlet. The OHRC said the deal was shaped by multiple roundtable discussions and input gathered from communities across Peel, Mississauga.com reports. Recommendations directed at Peel Regional Police include collecting race-based data, strengthening engagement with Black, Indigenous and other racialized communities, improving de-escalation training and internal accountability, and setting employment equity targets, the outlet notes.

items.title: Sixteen Mile Creek Gets a Third Automated Pumping Station as West Meadowvale Flood Fixes Continue
items.summary: According to INsauga, a community in northwest Mississauga that has dealt with severe flooding for years now has additional protection following the recent opening of what the city calls a critical piece of new infrastructure. The third automated pumping station built in the Lisgar area of west Meadowvale is now up and running, Ward 10 Councillor Sue McFadden told residents in an update this week, according to the outlet. INsauga reports the new station sits along Sixteen Mile Creek immediately south of Doug Leavens Boulevard and is now fully operational. The councillor's update comes as the city continues a broader flood mitigation effort in the area that has already delivered two earlier pumping stations, the outlet notes. INsauga reports a fourth facility remains on track to open in 2027, extending the flood protection program further across the neighbourhood.

items.title: Port Credit Parking Lot Near GO Station Could Become 288-Unit Rental Tower
items.summary: According to INsauga, a developer has proposed replacing a surface parking lot next to the Port Credit GO Station with a 26-storey rental apartment building. The proposal covers 12 and 26 Park Street, where a five-storey building and a seven-storey building would remain standing on the property while the new tower rises on the site's north portion, INsauga reports. The application was submitted by Sajecki Planning Inc. on behalf of Canahahns Company Limited to the City of Mississauga, according to the outlet, with the new building's entrance planned for Park Street East. INsauga reports the proposal calls for 288 total units, made up of 22 one-bedroom units, 169 one-bedroom-plus-den units, 57 two-bedroom units, nine two-bedroom-plus-den units and 31 three-bedroom units. Amenity space for residents is proposed on the building's seventh floor, the outlet notes.

items.title: Landlords Renovating Mississauga Rentals Will Need a City Licence Starting September 1
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city is introducing a new bylaw that requires landlords to obtain a municipal licence before renovating rental units, in a bid to stop so-called renovictions, where owners use renovation work as a pretext to evict tenants and reset rents. Under the Rental Repairs and Renovations Licensing Bylaw taking effect September 1, any landlord who issues a provincial N13 notice to vacate for major work must apply for a city licence within seven days, the outlet reports. Renovations cannot begin until the property owner holds both the city licence and a valid building permit, and applicants must show the unit genuinely needs to be vacated for the work, according to Mississauga.com. Licensed landlords will also be required to cover a one-time moving cost for displaced tenants, make monthly top-up payments during their temporary relocation and keep them updated on construction progress. Mississauga.com reports the city developed the bylaw through consultations with tenants, property owners and community groups, and landlords who do not comply will face municipal fines and enforcement action. The outlet notes the bylaw operates alongside existing provincial tenancy law, with the Landlord and Tenant Board retaining authority over eviction orders and tenancy disputes.

items.title: Canada's Largest Punjabi Arts Festival Comes to Ontario for the First Time in Mississauga
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, 5X Fest, billed as Canada's largest Punjabi arts and music organization, is bringing its flagship festival to Ontario for the first time in its 20-year history this weekend. The two-day event runs August 21 and 22 at the Small Arms Inspection Building on Lakeshore Road, according to a city news release cited by the outlet. Friday evening opens with a ticketed, all-ages indoor art party showcasing South Asian visual artists, including a featured artist talk with Inkquisitive, the artist name of Amandeep Singh. Mississauga.com reports Saturday's outdoor program shifts to live music, with performances from Punjabi artists, DJs and producers such as Deep Jandu, GMINXR, Signature by SB and J-Statik. Tickets for the festival are available through Showpass, the outlet notes, with taxes included in the listed price. The festival's arrival in Mississauga marks a milestone for an organization that has spent two decades building a following elsewhere before expanding into the province.

items.title: A Childhood Habit of Wandering Off Led This Mississauga Teen to Build a GPS Tracker for Neurodivergent Kids
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Ashwin Chunchu remembers slipping away from his parents as a seven-year-old, drawn toward a park or street without always knowing his way back, an experience he says is common among neurodivergent children. Now 17 and a recent Mississauga high school graduate, Chunchu has spent the months since March building StepSafe Kids, an affordable GPS tracker designed for children who wander or elope, and he says he wants to give other families the reassurance he wishes his own had. Mississauga.com reports his Kickstarter campaign has already surpassed its funding goal ahead of a September 3 deadline, with early pricing tiers offered as one-time payments with no recurring fees to the campaign's first 200 backers. The device is designed to clip onto clothing or attach to a lanyard for children with sensory sensitivities, and Chunchu expects it to reach the market in February 2027, according to the outlet. The project comes as Canada still has no federal or provincial database tracking elopement incidents and no emergency alert system equivalent to the Amber Alert for people at high risk of wandering, Mississauga.com reports. The outlet notes the recent death of 11 year old Parker Wells in Calgary has reignited national debate over these gaps in data, emergency alerting and public funding, leaving many families of autistic individuals to manage the risk largely on their own.
